title: Compatible derived comparisons for ordinary adic quotient models
statement: Let X,A,J,U,P,a,b satisfy the same hypotheses as lem-sfb-adic-perfect-reduction-models: X is a scheme, A a coefficient-universe commutative ring, J an ideal, U a coefficient pro-etale object with exact terminal evaluation on set sheaf epimorphisms, and P an integer cochain complex of finite projective A-modules strictly supported in [a,b]. With R_n,C_n,alpha_n and the actual completed constant derived object T as in def-sfb-adic-perfect-reduction-model-complexes, there exist isomorphisms r_n from the actual derived reductions rho_n(T) to Q(C_n). For every n, extend(tau_n)(r_(n+1)) followed by the universal K-flat computation comparison and Q(alpha_n) equals the actual derived balancing isomorphism at T followed by r_n. No K-projectivity assertion is included.

source.place: Tags 09C6 and 06YY; Tag 099M for successor scalar reassociation.

proof.text: Identify the actual local complex with the slice restriction of AdicPerfectModel.model by the existing proved constantPresentationIso and the functorial mapHomologicalComplex comparison. The existing private theorem AdicPerfectModel.model_kflat in AdicPerfectModelCompleteReduction gives K-flatness of the completed constant complex from the upper bound and projective terms. Apply ringedSite_restriction_exact_kflat and transport acyclicity of total tensor across the local chain isomorphism. This needs neither weak contractibility nor a lower bound.

The factorization mapDerivedCategoryFactors for exact overFunctor identifies the restriction of adicResidueConstantPerfect with Q of adicPerfectLocalComplex. Extend that isomorphism to level n and compose with the invertible K-flat computation counit supplied by derivedExtension. These composites define r_n. They use the given functors and their canonical counits, without choosing arbitrary witnesses.

Specialize adicFiniteExtendComp_existsUnique.choose_spec to the local K-flat complex, transporting the composite coefficient map along adicPerfectQuotientScalarStep_comp. This gives the normalized counit equation for exactly the ordinary balancing chain isomorphism adicPerfectQuotientStep. Naturality of adicFiniteExtendComp at the comparison from the actual restricted derived object to Q of the local complex transports that equation to T. Functoriality of maps and associativity of composition give the stated successor square.

lean.statement:
theorem adicPerfectReductionModels_compatibility (X : Scheme.{u})
    {A : Type (max v (u + 1))} [CommRing A] (J : Ideal A)
    (U : coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, v} X)
    (_hU : AdicResidueSliceWeaklyContractible.{u, v} X U)
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} A) ℤ)
    (a b : ℤ) (_ha : P.IsStrictlyGE a) (_hb : P.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (_hP : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (P.X i) ∧ Module.Projective A (P.X i)) :
    let R := fun n : ℕ ↦
      (finite (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A J n).over U
    let C : (n : ℕ) → Cx (R n) := fun n ↦ adicPerfectQuotientComplex.{u, v} X J U P n
    let R₀ := (completed (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A J).over U
    let ρ : (n : ℕ) → D R₀ ⥤ D (R n) := fun n ↦ adicResidueLocalReduction.{u, v} X J U n
    let T : D R₀ := (adicResidueRestriction
      (completed (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A J) U).obj
        (adicResidueConstantPerfect.{u, v} X J P)
    ∃ r : ∀ n : ℕ, (ρ n).obj T ≅ (Q (R n)).obj (C n),
      ∀ n : ℕ,
        (extend (adicPerfectQuotientScalarStep.{u, v} X J U n)).map (r (n + 1)).hom ≫
            (extendComparison (adicPerfectQuotientScalarStep.{u, v} X J U n)).app
              (C (n + 1)) ≫
            (Q (R n)).map (adicPerfectQuotientStep.{u, v} X J U P n).hom =
          (adicPerfectDerivedQuotientStep.{u, v} X J U n).hom.app T ≫ (r n).hom
